question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP tools/list request (jsonrpc 2.0, id 2, empty params) sent with NO mcp-session-id header, on a fresh connection after the initialize of p-20261020-harbor-mcp-initialize-keyless; Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.tool-names: list_workmap_tasks, get_cross_chain_report_quote, submit_paid_cross_chain_report, which are the three names the vendor's own llms.txt lists at its remote-MCP line
decoded.list_workmap_tasks: no required arguments; optional taskId and poolId, each a string of at most 100 characters; its description says it returns public instructions, submission links and non-cash Harbor Points and that it does not claim or submit work
decoded.get_cross_chain_report_quote: no properties and no required arguments; its description says it reads price, networks, batch size and payment destination and never initiates a payment
decoded.submit_paid_cross_chain_report: required txHash (0x and 64 hex), payerAddress (0x and 40 hex), addresses (1 to 5 unique 40-hex strings), signature (0x and 130 hex); optional paymentRailId, an enum of six values ethereum-usdc, base-usdc, arbitrum-usdc, polygon-usdc, ethereum-usdt, bsc-bsc-usd, defaulting to base-usdc; its description says it only submits a receipt and signature for verification and never pays, moves funds, approves a contract or signs for the user
decoded.paid-tool-not-called: the prober did not call submit_paid_cross_chain_report: it is a submission, and nothing in this pass sent a payment, a receipt or a signature

finding: A keyless tools/list with no session header answers 200 and lists exactly three tools, the three the vendor's llms.txt names: one free board reader, one quote reader, and one paid submission whose four required arguments are a transaction hash, a payer address, one to five addresses and a 65-byte personal_sign signature. Two of the three are readable by a stranger with no account; the third was deliberately not called. The registry entry names none of the three tools, so this record is where a reader can see what the keyless surface actually exposes. One IP is one sample, on 2026-10-20 at 18:08:03Z.
